quizzes.title: Constitutional and legal framework: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Census 2027 rests on a set of constitutional and legal provisions. The Union holds the power to conduct a census, and the count is connected with how seats in the Lok Sabha are distributed and how delimitation is handled after 2026. A separate central statute gives the exercise its legal mandate and decides whether residents must take part. The census is managed by a senior official who holds the posts of Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India. Its data also serves as a basis for updating the National Population Register and for preparing a register of citizens across the country. The same count is used for planning healthcare, education and infrastructure. Because it covers the whole population, the census provides a reference point against which other surveys can be measured. Phase I of the census is described as a house listing and housing census, and the exercise as a whole is described as the world's largest fully digital enumeration. The booklet also describes it as the first fully digital census in India. In that sense, the legal and administrative structure behind the count matters for representation, governance and welfare alike, and the framework connects a single national exercise to several different public purposes.

questions.q: On which census's data was Lok Sabha seat allocation frozen under the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the freeze uses 1971 Census data.

questions.q: Until when does that freeze on Lok Sabha seat allocation last?
options: Until the first census conducted after 2026
Until the first census conducted after 1971
Until the Census Act, 1948 is amended
Until the next Lok Sabha general election
questions.explanation: The booklet says the freeze lasts until the first census conducted after 2026.

questions.q: Who is named in the booklet as Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for Census 2027?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Mritunjay Kumar Narayan as Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

questions.q:
Consider the following.
Assertion (A): Articles 81 and 82 relate to Lok Sabha seat distribution and delimitation after 2026.
Reason (R): The Census Act, 1948 provides the legal mandate for the census and makes participation mandatory.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the Census Act is not the reason for the provisions of Articles 81 and 82.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 246 and Entry 69   ->   A. Union's power to conduct the census
II. 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002   ->   B. Freeze on Lok Sabha seat allocation
III. Articles 81 and 82   ->   C. Lok Sabha seat distribution and delimitation after 2026
IV. Census Act, 1948   ->   D. Legal mandate and mandatory participation
questions.explanation: Each provision in List I is paired with the function the booklet assigns to it in List II.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the legal framework.
I. The Union has power to conduct the census under Article 246 and Entry 69 of the Union List.
II. Lok Sabha seat allocation is frozen until the first census conducted after 1971.
III. The Census Act, 1948 makes participation in the census mandatory.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II gives the wrong end date for the freeze.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below about the legal framework are correct?
I. Articles 81 and 82 deal with Lok Sabha seat distribution and delimitation after 2026.
II. The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India is Vivek Joshi.
III. The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 froze seat allocation using 1971 Census data.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, and the booklet names Mritunjay Kumar Narayan rather than Vivek Joshi.

quizzes.title: Constitutional and legal framework: short answer
quizzes.passage: India's census draws its legal backing from more than one source. The Constitution places the power to conduct a census with the Union, and the relevant entry appears in the list of matters on which the Union may legislate. A central Act provides the statutory mandate and makes participation compulsory for those being counted. Separate constitutional provisions deal with how Lok Sabha seats are distributed and how constituencies are delimited after a fixed date. A constitutional amendment from the early 2000s holds Lok Sabha seat allocation on older census figures for a set period. The census is managed by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, a senior official whose name is given in the booklet. Results from the census also support the National Population Register, the planning of healthcare, education and infrastructure, and the work of other surveys, which can use the census as a benchmark. Taken together, these arrangements connect a national count to representation, administration and public planning in one legal framework. Each of these elements is set out separately in the booklet. Phase I of the census is a house listing and housing census, and the exercise is described as the world's largest fully digital enumeration.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Union get the power to conduct the census? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet cites Article 246, together with Entry 69 of the Union List, as the source of the census power.

questions.q: Which entry of the Union List covers the power to conduct the census? (entry number)
questions.explanation: The booklet pairs Article 246 with Entry 69 of the Union List.

questions.q: Which two Articles deal with Lok Sabha seat distribution and delimitation after 2026? (give the two numbers)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Articles 81 and 82 as covering Lok Sabha seat distribution and delimitation after 2026.

questions.q: In which year was the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act passed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act to 2002.

questions.q: In which year was the Census Act passed, giving the census its legal mandate? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Census Act, 1948 as the law that provides the legal mandate.

questions.q: According to the booklet, what is the surname of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India? (surname)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Mritunjay Kumar Narayan as Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

questions.q: The 84th Amendment froze Lok Sabha seat allocation using data from which census? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the freeze uses 1971 Census data.

quizzes.title: Purpose and challenges: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Census 2027 is designed to produce population information that policymakers can use across many areas. Caste is one of the categories for which information is gathered, and the booklet presents caste data as an input for targeting government programmes at marginalised groups. Census data is also used in electoral planning, including the allocation of seats. The exercise is large and is organised in phases, beginning with house listing and a housing census. Officials have to organise fieldwork across the country and coordinate with other agencies. The process also involves covering areas in the notified States and Union Territories. The exercise is described in the booklet as the world's largest fully digital enumeration, which relies on mobile applications and web-based data collection. The census is also described as a foundation for planning in several sectors, including the design of public services for growing and moving populations. Several practical and public difficulties accompany a count of this size, and the booklet discusses them alongside the purposes of the exercise. The booklet places the census in a long history of population counting, from ancient texts to colonial-era enumerations. Phase I is one step within the larger Census 2027 programme. The exercise is described as the world's largest population count.

questions.q: Which category does the booklet use for limited rural access to digital tools?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists limited rural access to digital tools as a technological challenge.

questions.q: Which two welfare schemes does the booklet name as examples that caste data could help sharpen?
options: PM Awas Yojana and Skill India
questions.explanation: The booklet names PM Awas Yojana and Skill India as schemes that caste data could sharpen.

questions.q:
Consider the following.
Assertion (A): Caste data aids delimitation and enables Women's One-Third Seat Reservation in Parliament and Assemblies.
Reason (R): Census forms are the basis for updating the National Population Register.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the NPR update is not the reason for the one-third seat reservation.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Data classification   ->   A. Avoiding duplication and inconsistencies in caste data
II. Logistical   ->   B. Large-scale training and coverage of remote areas
III. Administrative capacity   ->   C. Funds, staffing and inter-agency coordination
IV. Public trust   ->   D. Fears around NPR/NRC linkages
questions.explanation: Each challenge category in the booklet is paired with its matching description.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the purposes of Census 2027.
I. Unlike sample surveys, the census offers comprehensive population data.
II. The census is used only to count households and does not inform planning.
III. Demographic data from the census is vital for planning healthcare, education and infrastructure.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while statement II contradicts the booklet's account of planning uses.

questions.q:
Of the statements below, how many are correct?
I. Fears around NPR/NRC linkages are listed as a public trust challenge.
II. Census forms are used to prepare the Aadhaar number database.
III. The census is considered a reliable benchmark for other surveys.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, but the census forms are not said to prepare the Aadhaar database.

questions.q: Progress towards which global framework does the booklet say census data advances?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the census advances India towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

quizzes.title: Purpose and challenges: short answer
quizzes.passage: Caste data is one of the types of information that the census is expected to collect. The booklet presents it as useful for sharpening welfare programmes meant for marginalised groups, and as relevant to delimitation and to the representation of women in legislatures. Demographic information is also described as essential for planning services such as healthcare, education and infrastructure, particularly in view of urban migration and an ageing population. The census covers the whole population, which distinguishes it from smaller sample-based studies, and it is therefore used as a reference for other surveys. The booklet also notes that the census is linked with the updating of registers of residents and citizens. Carrying out the count is demanding, and officials must reach remote areas. Public trust is also a concern, particularly around links with other registers. The exercise must also avoid mistakes in how caste information is recorded. Finally, the census is expected to add to national progress on health, education and poverty indicators. The booklet traces population counting back to ancient texts and to colonial-era censuses.

questions.q: Which housing welfare scheme does the booklet name as one that caste data could sharpen? (scheme name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names PM Awas Yojana among the welfare schemes that caste data could sharpen.

questions.q: Besides PM Awas Yojana, which skills-focused scheme does the booklet name as one that caste data could sharpen? (scheme name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Skill India alongside PM Awas Yojana.

questions.q: What fraction of seats in Parliament and Assemblies does Women's One-Third Seat Reservation cover? (fraction)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the reservation as Women's One-Third Seat Reservation in Parliament and Assemblies.

questions.q: Which challenge category covers duplication and inconsistencies in caste data? (category name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists duplication and inconsistencies in caste data under data classification.

questions.q: Which challenge category covers large-scale training and coverage of remote areas? (category name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists large-scale training and coverage of remote areas as a logistical challenge.

questions.q: Which challenge category covers funds, staffing and inter-agency coordination? (category name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists funds, staffing and inter-agency coordination under administrative capacity.

questions.q: Progress towards which global framework does census data help advance? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet says census data advances India towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

quizzes.title: NPR, CAA and NRC: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Three terms are often discussed together in the context of Census 2027: the National Population Register, the Citizenship Amendment Act and the National Register of Citizens. Each one has a different purpose and a different scope. The first is a database and is connected with the census exercise. The second deals with refugees who came to India from neighbouring countries and belong to particular religious communities. The third concerns the citizens of India and the documents that establish their status. Public discussion has raised questions about whether a population database is needed alongside the Aadhaar number, and the government's response has been that the two serve different objectives. The Census Act provides the legal framework within which the census operates. The three terms are sometimes treated as one issue, although each covers a different group of people. The booklet presents a comparison table to show the scope, coverage and purpose of each, and it discusses these terms as part of the wider debate on the census.

questions.q: Which register is described as a database of every resident, including foreigners?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the National Population Register as a database of every resident, including foreigners.

questions.q: By what date must the minority refugees covered under the CAA have come to India?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the CAA covers minority refugees who came to India before 31 December 2014.

questions.q: Which of the following religious communities is NOT listed among the minority refugees covered under the CAA?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Hindu, Christian, Sikh, Parsi, Jain and Buddhist, and does not list Jewish.

questions.q:
Consider the following.
Assertion (A): The NRC covers citizens of India who have valid identity documents.
Reason (R): The NPR covers every resident, including foreigners.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the NPR's coverage of foreigners does not explain the NRC's scope.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. National Population Register   ->   A. Minority refugees from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh
II. Citizenship Amendment Act   ->   B. Citizens of India with valid identity documents
III. National Register of Citizens   ->   C. Database of every resident, including foreigners
IV. Government's reply on the absence of Muslims   ->   D. Muslims are not a minority in the three neighbouring countries
questions.explanation: Each register or law in List I is matched with the scope or reply the booklet gives for it in List II.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the registers and the CAA.
I. The NPR covers residents who have lived at an address for the last 6 months and will stay there for the next 6 months.
II. The CAA covers Muslim refugees from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh.
III. The NRC covers citizens of India with valid identity documents.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because the CAA covers listed non-Muslim minority refugees.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below about the registers are correct?
I. Census forms are the basis for updating the National Population Register.
II. The CAA covers refugees who came to India after 31 December 2014.
III. The National Population Register is meant to be used for government schemes.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while statement II reverses the 31 December 2014 cut-off.

quizzes.title: NPR, CAA and NRC: short answer
quizzes.passage: Census 2027 is discussed alongside three other exercises that are often confused with it. The first is a national database of residents, which is linked to the census through the forms used to update it. The second is a law that concerns refugees who entered India from neighbouring countries and belong to certain religious communities, and it sets a date by which they must have arrived. The third is a list of people who are citizens of India and hold valid identity documents, and only one state is described as updating it. Concerns have been raised that the database overlaps with another national identity system, but the government has argued that the two have different aims. The Census Act provides the legal framework within which the census operates, and the Union government conducts it. The census itself covers the whole population and is organised in phases, with house listing first. The booklet presents these three exercises as distinct, with different coverage and purposes.

questions.q: For how many months must a person have lived at an address in the past to be covered by the database of residents? (number of months)
questions.explanation: The booklet says coverage requires residence at an address for the last 6 months.

questions.q: By what date must minority refugees have come to India to be covered by the law? (date)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 31 December 2014 as the arrival cut-off for minority refugees under the law.

questions.q: How many neighbouring countries are named as sources of minority refugees under the law? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh as the three neighbouring countries.

questions.q: What is the short form of the law covering minority refugees from neighbouring countries? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet refers to the law covering these refugees as the CAA.

questions.q: What is the short form of the register of citizens of India who hold valid identity documents? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the NRC as covering citizens of India with valid identity documents.

questions.q: The government says the database of residents does not duplicate which other national identity system? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet records the government's view that there is no duplication between the NPR and Aadhaar.

questions.q: Which register covers every resident, including foreigners? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the NPR as a database of every resident, including foreigners.
